cita: Kannabhiran (2026). Institutional Memory as Organizational Knowledge: AI Agents That Learn Their Jobs from Experience, Not Instructions.
problema: Self-published case study arguing that domain expertise, organizational protocols, and quality standards encoded in long expert prompts (50-200 lines) can instead be externalized into a governed, consensus-validated institutional-memory store, letting individual agents run on minimal (3-line) role prompts and letting agents WRITE back what they learn for future agents to reuse.
mecanismo: 11 agents across 5 departments each hold only a 3-line role prompt; all domain expertise/protocols/history live in (S)AGE, a 4-node BFT-consensus knowledge base with department-scoped RBAC (clearance 1-3) queried via domain-tagged similarity search. A declarative routing table (20+ states) drives an event-driven agent mesh (design->harden->calibrate->quality->red-team-solve). After an independent blind-solve, the CEO agent WRITEs a pentest-report observation back to (S)AGE; it is validated by weighted BFT consensus (score=0.88) and becomes queryable institutional memory for all future agents -- i.e. write-back of measured operational experience gated by multi-node consensus rather than a single agent's unverified self-report.
evaluacion: A single self-run case study/demo (not a controlled benchmark): one full pipeline run (508s, 13 stages) producing one AES-CBC Padding-Oracle CTF challenge, one independent blind-solve by a separate agent (525.2s, 16,384 oracle queries via a self-optimized C-compiled solver), an 11-agent qualitative 'identity verification' test (6 questions each), and one closed-loop write-back to institutional memory (consensus score 0.88); no baselines, no repeated trials, no statistical testing.
numeros_clave: 11 agents/5 departments, 3-line prompts; pipeline 508s -> quality 93.0/100, calibration gap 0.20; blind solve 525.2s / 16,384 oracle queries (10x->18x solver speedup across 3 iterations); consensus validation score 0.88 (4-node BFT); identity verification 11/11 agents correct.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The CEO agent's pentest-report write-back becoming a durable, queryable lesson for future hardeners/calibrators/designers (S4.4 'Feedback Loop Closure') is a direct instance of MF's promotion-of-experience-to-durable-recipe need.
Gating new memory admission on 4-node weighted BFT consensus (score=0.88) before it becomes queryable (S4.4) is a concrete write-admission provenance mechanism MF could adapt.

notes: RECONSIDERAR: single-author, self-published technical report (arXiv:submit, not a refereed venue), n=1 anecdotal pipeline run on a fictional company testing the author's own commercial platform (levelupctf.com); epistemic caveats on emergent expertise are acknowledged in S4.2 itself.

cita: Kannabhiran (2026). Consensus-Validated Memory Improves Agent Performance on Complex Tasks.
problema: Multi-agent LLM systems are stateless across invocations, so institutional knowledge (e.g. 'AES-ECB challenges consistently under-calibrate') is lost between runs; existing memory systems (Mem0/MemOS/Collaborative Memory/Reflexion/MemGPT) provide persistence but no GOVERNANCE over what gets written, no verifiable provenance, and no protection against knowledge pollution -- and no prior work measured whether governed memory actually improves downstream TASK performance rather than just retrieval-layer properties.
mecanismo: (S)AGE distills an agent's raw observation via a local LLM into a novelty-aware summary (only net-new insights vs existing knowledge), proposes it as a memory candidate (768-dim embedding + domain tag) to a 4-node BFT validator network using Proof-of-Experience weighted voting (weight = historical accuracy + domain relevance + recency + corroboration); only proposals reaching a >=2/3 weighted quorum are WRITE-committed, confidence decays exponentially thereafter, and future agents RETRIEVE by domain+embedding similarity restricted to consensus-validated memories.
evaluacion: Controlled experiments on an AI CTF-generation pipeline (9 agents): sequential no-memory control vs (S)AGE-ON treatment (paired N=20 crypto_aes runs, N=15 sqli cross-category, N=50 sqli sequential-baseline control), Mann-Whitney U + Cohen's d + OLS regression (implemented from scratch, no scipy), dual independent LLM evaluators (cold vs memory-augmented) to control evaluator bias, a 3-level prompt-ablation (minimal/guided/onboarding) crossed with knowledge-seeding, and a cross-domain contamination test.
numeros_clave: 40% lower calibration error with (S)AGE (mean gap 0.282 vs 0.468, n=20/arm, Cohen's d=-0.824 LARGE); quality std 0.0 (all 93.0) vs vanilla mean 90.1/std 13.1; onboarding+seeded prompt achieved perfect calibration (gap=0.0) vs expert 120-line prompt's best 0.10/20 runs; 50-run sequential baseline variance collapse stdev 0.159->0.113; cross-domain filtering rejected stale memories 14/14 (100%) at scores 0.35-0.50 vs accepted relevant ones at 0.59-0.86.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The explicit warning seed 'Padding Oracle attacks consistently calibrate at 1.2-1.8 regardless of obfuscation' (S4.5.4) plus the discovered echo-chamber failure mode is a concrete case of curating negative/cautionary knowledge and diversity-seeding to prevent one narrow lesson from crowding out others.

The cross-domain filtering experiment (14/14 stale memories rejected at 0.35-0.50 vs domain-relevant accepted at 0.59-0.86, S4.4) empirically confirms MF's premise that write-admission needs an active provenance/relevance gate, not just accumulation.

The full (S)AGE pipeline -- raw observation -> novelty-aware summary -> BFT-validated commit -> queryable knowledge -- is exactly MF's promotion-of-transient-experience-to-durable-recipe pattern, measured here via 20-run convergence (S4.1).

notes: RECONSIDERAR: same author/platform as W7133488000 and W7133519884 (self-published Technical Report, not peer-reviewed, evaluated on the author's own commercial CTF product); statistics are unusually rigorous (Mann-Whitney/Cohen's d, honest null findings, echo-chamber failure reported) for a self-published venue -- see S4.1/S4.4/S4.5.3.

cita: Kannabhiran (2026). Agent Memory Infrastructure: Byzantine-Resilient Institutional Memory for Multi-Agent Systems.
problema: Existing agent-memory systems (Mem0, MemOS, Collaborative Memory, MemGPT, Reflexion) provide persistence but lack GOVERNANCE over collectively-held knowledge: no consensus-validated organization-wide accumulation, no cryptographically verifiable provenance, no formal dispute/rollback authority, and no Byzantine-resilient validation of agent-generated knowledge artifacts -- creating fragility (poisoning, sybil attacks, cross-domain contamination) in regulated/adversarial multi-agent deployments.
mecanismo: Each memory object carries natural-language text + RDF-compatible graph triples + an embedding + the proposer's cryptographic signature + rich provenance metadata (domain, timestamp, confidence, corroboration count, parent-revision hash-pointer for append-only versioning, TTL, access-control scope). WRITE admission runs through Proof-of-Experience: each validator's vote weight is a geometric mean of 4 bounded factors (historical-accuracy EWMA, domain-relevance cosine similarity, activity-recency decay, corroboration-strength log-scale), capped so no validator exceeds ~10% of weight; a memory commits only at >=2/3 weighted quorum, confidence then decays exponentially unless corroborated, and a human Governance Authority retains veto/rollback outside the BFT layer. Older corroborated memories are periodically distilled into higher-level 'meta-memories' (CONSOLIDACION) that supersede but keep parent pointers to constituents.
evaluacion: Production implementation on a 4-node CometBFT+custom-ABCI network, PostgreSQL16+pgvector (HNSW) off-chain store, 33 REST endpoints; load/fault-tolerance testing (956 req/s submissions, 21.6ms P95 queries, 0% error; 1-of-4 node failure tolerated, 2-of-4 halts consensus) plus 94 automated tests; a controlled empirical proof-of-concept on the author's 'Level Up' CTF multi-agent platform comparing (S)AGE-backed vs memoryless calibration accuracy.
numeros_clave: Calibration accuracy ~2x better than memoryless baseline (Cohen's d=-0.860, large effect, advantage grows with task complexity); production load: 956 req/s submissions, 21.6ms P95 query latency, 0% error rate; BFT verified: 1-of-4 node failure tolerated, 2-of-4 halts consensus (correct); 94 automated tests (48 Go unit, 15 integration, 3 Byzantine, 21 SDK).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Hierarchical distillation of 'frequently-corroborated memories...into higher-level abstractions (meta-memories)' (S6), inspired by Complementary Learning Systems and retaining parent pointers, is a directly transferable pattern for MF's promotion-of-gotchas-to-durable-recipes need.

The explicit threat model (S5: memory poisoning/sybil/prompt-injection-via-memory/cross-domain contamination/institutional drift) with per-vector mitigations formalizes exactly the provenance/staleness/poisoning risks MF's FIDELIDAD anchor targets.
Hot->Warm->Cold compression/archival tiers by age/access-frequency/confidence (S6) is a concrete cache-tiering scheme MF could adapt for its derived-index-as-cache design.

notes: RECONSIDERAR: same author/platform/venue concerns as W7133488000 and W7133508550 (self-published Technical Report, non-peer-reviewed, dhillon@levelupctf.com). Formal spec in S3-S4 (PoE formula, quorum rule); production metrics in S10.

cita: Bhardwaj (2026). SuperLocalMemory: Privacy-Preserving Multi-Agent Memory with Bayesian Trust Defense Against Memory Poisoning.
problema: Persistent multi-agent memory inherits persistent vulnerabilities: cloud-default memory systems (Mem0, MemOS) create centralized multi-tenant attack surfaces for OWASP ASI06 memory poisoning (documented real attacks: Gemini Memory exploit, calendar-invite poisoning at 73% success, Lakera sleeper-agent), and none of them provide trust scoring or poisoning defense; even 'local' competitors still require heavy cloud-like infra (Docker/Postgres/Qdrant).
mecanismo: A four-layer local-first stack (SQLite+FTS5 storage -> hierarchical materialized-path index -> Leiden-clustered TF-IDF knowledge graph -> Beta-Binomial pattern learning) with per-memory provenance (created_by, source_protocol, trust_score-at-write, JSON provenance_chain). A Bayesian trust scorer evolves each agent's trust t via t_{i+1}=t_i+delta*1/(1+n*eta) from asymmetric positive/negative behavioral signals (negative signals weighted larger), blocking WRITE/delete for agents below trust<0.3 -- a continuous, decaying ADMISION gate rather than a one-shot check. A separate zero-LLM adaptive re-ranking layer (rule-based, then LambdaRank-trained GBDT) re-ranks RETRIEVAL results from learned behavioral preferences, with behavioral data isolated in a GDPR-erasable database.
evaluacion: Seven benchmark dimensions on Apple M4 Pro: search-latency vs DB size, concurrent-write throughput (1/2/5/10 writers), knowledge-graph scaling, a 5-configuration layer-ablation study (MRR/NDCG@5/NDCG@10), Bayesian trust scoring under 3 adversarial scenarios (benign/single-poisoner/sleeper, 200 ops x10 agents), a small human pilot (1 developer, 20 queries/70 relevance judgments), and a qualitative comparison table vs Mem0/MemOS/A-MEM/Cognee/Zep/Letta.
numeros_clave: 10.6ms median search latency @100 memories (Table 1); trust separation gap=0.90, sleeper-agent trust degradation 72.4% (0.902->0.249, Table 4); adaptive re-ranking NDCG@5 +104% (0.441->0.900, +20ms overhead, Table 3); concurrent writes: 220 ops/sec peak @2 agents, 0 lock errors across 1/2/5/10 writers (Table 2); 1.4KB/memory storage at 10K scale.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Per-memory provenance_chain plus Bayesian trust scoring that gates WRITE access below a threshold is a concrete, measured (trust gap 0.90, 72% sleeper degradation, Table 4) mechanism for the provenance/poisoning concern MF's FIDELIDAD anchor targets.

The rule-based-then-ML adaptive re-ranker, gated by accumulated feedback-signal count (Phase 0/1/2, S3.3), delivers a measured +104% NDCG@5 gain (Table 3), supporting MF's measured/tiered-retrieval stance over naive always-retrieve.

The re-ranking and trust-scoring gains are achieved with zero LLM inference calls and only +20ms latency overhead (S3.3, Table 3), a concrete low-cost pattern for a context-economy-conscious memory layer.

notes: Independent researcher preprint (under review) but methodologically transparent, including an explicit 'evaluation circularity note' (S5.5) about NDCG labels overlapping ranker features. Key tables: 1-4, S5.

cita: Maio (2026). mnemos: Biomimetic Memory Architectures for Large Language Model Agents.
problema: Current agentic memory systems (Mem0, Zep/Graphiti, Letta/MemGPT) are append-only vector stores that never filter noise AT INGESTION and retrieve by flat cosine similarity alone, ignoring cognitive/emotional context and associative structure; LongMemEval shows even the best commercial systems reach only 30-70% accuracy with 30-60% degradation as history scales.
mecanismo: A 3-phase (encode/retrieve/maintain) pipeline composes 5 neuroscience-inspired modules: a SurprisalGate filters WRITE-time noise via LLM-predicted next-intent vs actual-input prediction error (only surprisal>tau=0.3 default is stored); an AffectiveRouter tags a 3-axis cognitive-state vector (valence/arousal/complexity) at write time and blends it (0.7 semantic + 0.3 state-distance) into RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO scoring; MutableRAG reconsolidates retrieved chunks (flags as labile, async LLM-checks for contradiction, overwrites in-place with a version increment + revision history), solving the stale-fact problem; SpreadingActivation retrieves an associative neighborhood via BFS energy propagation over a similarity graph instead of point k-NN; a SleepDaemon periodically consolidates the episodic buffer into durable semantic facts (CONSOLIDACION), pruning raw logs; a write-time safety firewall blocks/redacts secrets and PII at every ingestion point.
evaluacion: Controlled ablation studies using mock LLM/embedding providers to isolate architectural effects (not real-model benchmarks): surprisal-threshold sweep on 15 interactions, affective-routing retrieval on 9 tagged chunks across 3 states, spreading-activation decay sweep on a synthetic 4-node concept chain, reconsolidation on a single simulated contradiction, sleep-consolidation compression across buffer sizes (5-50 episodes), and a 10-interaction full-pipeline integration test; qualitative architectural comparison vs Mem0/Zep/LangMem/Letta; no head-to-head benchmark (e.g. LongMemEval) against competitors is run (explicitly deferred to future work).
numeros_clave: Sleep consolidation: 50 episodes -> 3 facts (16.7x compression, superlinear with buffer size); spreading activation reaches 4/4 nodes at default decay=0.2 vs 1/4 at decay=0.9; surprisal gate storage rate 87% (tau 0-0.4) -> 60% (tau=0.9) -> 27% (tau=1.0); full-pipeline test stores 8/10 interactions (filters filler); affective routing achieves 3/3 correct state-congruent retrieval per state.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The SleepDaemon's periodic consolidation of episodic buffer into durable semantic facts (16.7x superlinear compression, Fig.4) is a directly measured instance of MF's promotion-of-transient-interactions-into-durable-recipes need.

The SurprisalGate is a concrete discretionary WRITE trigger keyed on prediction error rather than write-everything, with a measured storage-rate-vs-threshold curve (Fig.2) directly extending MF's G-M1 need.

notes: Ablations use MockLLMProvider/synthetic embeddings (not real models), a caveat the paper itself acknowledges (S 'Limitations'); see Fig.2 (threshold sweep) and Fig.4 (compression).

cita: Singhal (2026). ForgetAgent: Verifiable Deletion in Multi-Layer Memory Architectures for LLM Agents.
problema: Agent memory spans embeddings, structured records, caches, derived entities, and tool transcripts, so deleting a memory item from one layer does not guarantee it is unrecoverable -- adversaries can reconstruct deleted facts via paraphrase queries, embedding-neighborhood leakage, tool-transcript traces, or story-completion/multi-hop inference, leaving no formal guarantee that OLVIDO (right-to-be-forgotten/GDPR/CCPA compliance) actually removed the information.
mecanismo: Formalizes deletion as counterfactual indistinguishability (an adversary cannot tell post-deletion state M' from a counterfactual M^-Df that never had the forget-set) plus a weaker (eps,delta)-recovery-security notion, over a dependency-closed forget-set D_f+ = D_f union Dep(D_f) covering all summaries/derived-entities/cached-behaviors causally dependent on the deleted item. A 7-layer deletion pipeline operationalizes this: identify all instantiations via structured lookup + embedding-neighborhood search (cosine distance <0.05) + a DFS dependency graph over caches/transcripts, purge raw storage, purge/reweight embeddings (tombstones), invalidate caches/derived entities, sanitize tool transcripts, emit a cryptographic deletion receipt (attestation, not a formal irrecoverability proof), then run automated red-team attacks (membership inference, paraphrase retrieval, neighbor leakage, transcript analysis, story-completion) to empirically verify no residual leakage, rolling back + alerting on failure.
evaluacion: ForgetAgentBench, a released synthetic benchmark of 500 agent interactions with 1,500 labeled deletion targets (personal/preference/domain-specific, multiple difficulty levels); compares 5 deletion strategies (naive vs the full 7-layer method) measuring red-team-attack robustness and a retained-task utility ratio; the authors explicitly caveat that results are limited to synthetic benchmark settings (no real deployed-agent evaluation).
numeros_clave: Naive deletion: 18% robustness to red-team attacks. Full 7-layer method: 94% robustness with 97% retained task utility (ForgetAgentBench, 500 interactions/1,500 deletion targets); embedding-neighborhood identification uses cosine-distance threshold 0.05.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The formal (eps,delta)-recovery-security definition plus the dependency-closure D_f+ = D_f union Dep(D_f) (S III.D) offers a rigorous, transferable notion of 'is this fact actually gone' -- including derived-entity/cache descendants -- that MF's FIDELIDAD anchor could adopt as a test.

The threat model's M={E,S,C,D,T} -- a single fact instantiated across embeddings/SQL/caches/derived-entities/transcripts, where clearing one layer still leaks via others (S I.A) -- directly confirms MF's COSTURAS concern about single-source-per-fact vs multi-store seams.

notes: RECONSIDERAR: published in IJRASET (a low-selectivity engineering journal), single author affiliated with 'Empros International School, Pune' (a secondary school), suggesting a student paper rather than a standard peer-reviewed venue -- despite a well-formalized threat model (S III).
